summary:
Lublin Voivodeship, in south-eastern Poland, stands under the Polish national framework: passport and marker rules, conditions in custody, and hate-crime provisions are set nationally and are carried by the national assessment. What is specific to the voivodeship is its own record of official hostility.

Świdnik, a town in the voivodeship, was the first place in Poland to adopt an "LGBT-free" declaration. Its county council passed the resolution in March 2019, pledging to shield children from "homosexual propaganda" and to refrain from actions encouraging "tolerance of LGBT people". The text is non-binding; it does not itself restrict a visitor's movement or access to services, and it records the posture of a local authority rather than a rule enforceable against anyone.

The voivodeship legislature adopted a comparable declaration of its own and, when the matter was revisited, voted to keep it in place. It repealed the resolution on 20 September 2021, after the European Commission threatened to withhold funding from voivodeships that retained such declarations. The repeal changed the regional assembly's formal position. Whether the county-level declarations, including Świdnik's, were withdrawn is not established by these sources.
tangentialFactors: The 2021 repeal followed funding conditionality from the European Commission rather than any documented reversal of local political opinion: the voivodeship assembly had voted to keep its declaration before it voted to repeal it. Formal withdrawal of a declaration therefore does not establish that local government practice toward LGBT residents changed.
localsOnly: The declarations were pledges by local and regional authorities about their own conduct. The Świdnik county resolution committed the council to protect children from what it called "homosexual propaganda" and to refrain from actions encouraging tolerance of LGBT people, commitments about the council's own activities rather than rules binding residents. Residents in that county would have had no local-government sponsorship of LGBT-related initiatives, and the voivodeship assembly's vote to retain its declaration before repealing it under funding pressure indicates that the local political composition supporting it was unchanged at the time of repeal.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the county-level declarations, Świdnik's among them, were ever repealed or remain on the books is not established in these sources; the repeals documented here are at regional level. This inventory contains no region-specific account of violence, prosecution, policing or enforcement in Lublin Voivodeship, and no region-specific data on custody, healthcare access or document handling; those matters belong to the national assessment.
